## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">PSAT/SAT Test Administration
• Since 2017 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
 administered the PSAT as part of the spring test administration
 to 10th graders
• Since 2018 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
 administered the SAT to 11th graders.
• Both the PSAT and SAT include sections in ELA and
 Mathematics.

 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Transition to Digital SAT
• In 2024, the College Board transitioned to the Digital SAT
 administration platform.
• Several aspects of the assessment changed during this transition in
 terms of both user facing features (computer versus P&amp;P
 administration) as well as backend features (adaptive versus fixed-
 form).
• Changes in the results in 2024 from 2023 led to concern amongst
 some states about test equivalence.
• The analyses in this presentation are intended to support discussions
 about the equivalence of tests and comparability of results.

 4</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Introduction
• We examine student performance on the PSAT/SAT in several ways
 • Participation frequencies
 • Mean/Standard Deviations of Scores by year
 • Mean/Median Baseline SGP by year (SAT only)
 • Baseline SGPs are normed using pre-pandemic, PSAT-SAT growth
 norms.

 Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 6</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Frequencies
• In general, there was a substantial decrease in participation due to the
 pandemic.
• For the PSAT, the number of students tested has roughly returned to pre-
 pandemic level.
• For the SAT, in 2024 there was a substantial (approximate 8%) increase in
 the number of students tested.

 Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 8</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/14.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Summary Measures
• Both ELA and Mathematics PSAT saw decreases in mean scaled score over
 the last six years. The drop in mathematics in 2023-2024 from 436.4 to
 418.4 was particularly large.
• Both ELA and Mathematics PSAT saw increases in the standard deviation in
 2023-2024 from prior years.
• Both ELA and Mathematics SAT saw decreases in mean scaled score,
 particularly in 2023-2024. Mathematics dropped from 461.5 to 445.9.
• Both ELA and Mathematics SAT saw increases in standard deviation in
 2023-2024.
• The number of LOSS (200) scores in the SAT saw a large increase in
 2023-2024.

 Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 14</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/18.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Baseline SGPs
• Because growth conditions on prior scores, baseline SGPs are much more
 robust to changes in the population of students tested than status
 measures.
• Baseline SGPs were fairly stable across the last several years in ELA, less so
 in mathematics. The drop in the mean SGP to 44.4 in 2023-2024 in
 mathematics is synonymous with the drop in achievement observed.
• The low median SGP in mathematics was caused (largely) by low SGPs of
 students in the 6th, 7th, and 8th prior score deciles.
• The Center works with another state using the PSAT/SAT tests in high school
 and observed a very similar pattern (as evidenced by the following two
 goodness of fit plots)

 Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 18</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/21.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Conclusions
• Results comparing 2023-2024 SAT results with prior years indicates
 discrepancies in mathematics which suggest assessment changes may have
• In general, assessment changes are always accompanied by score
 discrepancies such as those observed here.
• Drawing firm causal conclusions isn’t substantiated with these secondary
 analyses. However, further investigations into digital SAT test format —
 particularly for higher achieving students where lower growth was observed
 — may lead to causal factors leading to lower scores.

 Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 21</div>
```
